brief: An 8-second five-day weather forecast: columns for Mon to Fri appear left to right with a stagger; each has a simple icon drawn with shapes (sun, cloud, rain, sun, storm), the high temperature above and the low below (72/58, 68/55, 61/50, 75/60, 64/52).
checks: The leftmost visible column when it first appears is for Monday and shows a sun icon (simple shape‑based sun) with the high temperature "72" above it and the low temperature "58" below it.
The second column from the left when it appears is for Tuesday and shows a cloud icon with high "68" above and low "55" below.
The third column when it appears is for Wednesday and shows a rain icon with high "61" above and low "50" below.
The fourth column when it appears is for Thursday and shows a sun icon with high "75" above and low "60" below.
The fifth column when it appears is for Friday and shows a storm icon with high "64" above and low "52" below.
Each column appears sequentially from left to right with a noticeable delay between the appearance of adjacent columns (no two columns appear at the exact same frame).
All animated properties (position, scale, opacity) of the columns use smooth ease‑in and ease‑out curves rather than linear motion.
There is at least one visible change (appearance, movement, or transformation) in every one‑second interval of the video, ensuring no dead air.
No visual element appears before the 0.5‑second mark; the first column begins to appear at or after 0.5 s.
After the last column has fully appeared, the final composition remains static (no further animation) for at least 0.5 seconds before the video ends.
All columns are horizontally aligned on a common baseline and evenly spaced with equal gutters between them; none of the icons or text touch or cross the outer frame edges.
The text (temperature numbers) is large enough to be easily readable (approximately at least one‑tenth of the frame height) and has high contrast against its background.
The color palette used for the icons and text is harmonious (no clashing hues) and there are no visible rendering glitches, flicker, overlapping text, or artifacts.
The video fills the entire frame with no black bars, borders, masks, or hard‑edged vignettes; the picture extends to the edges of the viewport.
